title: Flock media-relations role describes a success-story publicity pipeline
finding: The role solicits customer stories, drafts press releases, pitches news outlets, supports press conferences, and seeks a high volume of positive press coverage each week.

title: Flock asks customers to become public advocates
finding: The program asks customers to volunteer for a case study, news pitch, quote, referral, or event—documenting a formal mechanism for turning customer outcomes into marketing and press material.

title: Records show Flock supplying copy-ready talking points to a police chief
finding: A Virginia investigation reports that a Flock executive gave a chief scripted responses and said the text could be forwarded as-is or copied into a public memo.

title: Flock publishes sample social-media and email copy
finding: The resource provides ready-made promotional language. The page is aimed mainly at residential and community customers, so it should not be represented as a police-department template without additional records.

title: Flock describes sponsored trade-publication content as part of its marketing strategy
finding: A procurement response lists sponsored content, trade-publication advertising, social content, email campaigns, and webinars among its marketing channels.

title: Flock distributes company-authored stories through GlobeNewswire
finding: Paid wire distribution is documented and disclosed. It is evidence of press-release promotion—not evidence that an independent newsroom was secretly paid.
